record.paper_title: A General Framework for Coloring Problems: Old Results, New Results, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let G be a triangle-free graph with chromatic number chi(G), and let T be a spanning tree of G used as a backbone. A backbone coloring is a proper vertex coloring of G in which endpoints of every edge of T receive colors that differ by at least 2, and bbc(G,T) is the smallest number of colors needed. Does there exist a universal small constant c such that bbc(G,T) <= chi(G) + c for every triangle-free graph G and every spanning tree T?

evidence.quote: Does there exist a small constant c such that bbc(G,T) <= chi(G)+c holds for all triangle-free graphs G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph, and let $T=(V,E_T)$ be a spanning tree of $G$ (so $E_T\subseteq E$). A backbone coloring of $(G,T)$ is a map $c:V\to\{1,2,\dots,k\}$ such that:
(i) $|c(u)-c(v)|\geq 1$ for every edge $uv\in E$ (proper coloring of $G$), and
(ii) $|c(u)-c(v)|\geq 2$ for every edge $uv\in E_T$.
The backbone chromatic number $\mathrm{bbc}(G,T)$ is the smallest $k$ for which such a coloring exists. Let $\chi(G)$ denote the ordinary chromatic number of $G$, and call $G$ triangle-free if it contains no $K_3$ subgraph.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mathrm{bbc}(G,T)\leq \chi(G)+c$$
holds for every triangle-free graph $G$ and every spanning tree $T$ of $G$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered negatively. Using generalized Mycielski-type constructions, one can produce triangle-free graphs $R_n$ with spanning trees $T_n$ satisfying $\mathrm{bbc}(R_n,T_n)=2\chi(R_n)-1$, so no universal additive constant $c$ exists. This was established in work on backbone colorings and generalized Mycielski graphs (Araujo, Nešetřil, et al., SIAM J. Discrete Math.).

status_evidence.title: Backbone Colorings and Generalized Mycielski Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of triangle-free graphs R_n with spanning trees T_n such that BBC(R_n,T_n) = 2χ(R_n) − 1.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture fails: there is no constant c with bbc(G,T) ≤ χ(G)+c for all triangle-free G and spanning trees T.

status_evidence.title: Backbone Colorings of Graphs (West problem page)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the Broersma et al. question about additive constant bound for triangle-free graphs and its resolution.
status_evidence.claim: The question asked by Broersma et al. for triangle-free graphs was answered in the negative.
